digest.component_or_area: reconciler write seam / git mutation gate
propositions: The existing checker (policy d37e) enforces mechanism rules (no raw subprocess git) but misses protocol violations (mutations outside atomic transactions) because it sanctions git-adapter mutation primitives at module granularity, allowing callers to compose them into non-atomic sequences.

Rule R3 must fire on calls to git-adapter mutation primitives (add, commit, commit_tree, read_tree, rm_cached, update_ref, write_tree) made from outside the sanctioned seam files (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py), using receiver-based binding to distinguish git-adapter calls from unrelated .add()/.commit() patterns.

Two out-of-transaction sites must carry durable reasoned inline markers rather than debt: reconcile_helpers.py's _commit_binding_store_snapshot (selective staging boundary) and _pass_lock_lifecycle.py's _purge_committed_reconciler_locks (detached-index CAS safety).

The rule must correctly resolve git-adapter receiver bindings from both import forms (from rebar_reconciler import git_adapter) and dynamic-loader patterns (git_adapter = _load(...)), while avoiding false positives on non-git-adapter .add()/.commit() calls and read-only exports.

R3 integration into the existing checker keeps one gate, one marker vocabulary, and one CI wiring, reusing the existing # raw-git-ok: reason marker syntax (with mandatory reason) for both R1/R2 and R3 violations.

The rule must not fire inside the three sanctioned seam files themselves (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py), which ARE the atomic transaction where primitives are legally composed under the ref lock.
